exposure.rater_type: AI; no human rater or human validation
exposure.model: GPT-6 family; shared AI/default model context; exact model identifier and build not exposed
exposure.tool_versions: functions.exec, exec_command/python3, web.run; exact tool builds not exposed
provided_materials: parent annotation task and durable GitHub preference
exposure.prior_rating_summary_seen: Only the aggregate v1 summary printed in the allowed v2 protocol; no case-level v1 labels or scopes accessed.

primary_source_access.ramsoy_overgaard_2004: Retrieved original author-uploaded PDF; inspected printed pp.11–12 including Table 2 and typical report.
primary_source_access.lutz_2002: Retrieved original article PDF mirror; inspected printed pp.1587–1588 training and cluster passages.
primary_source_access.chuyin_v3: Attempted exact version-3 URL twice through web.run; retrieval failed with HTTP 403; Methods and Figure 4 not inspected.

exposure.independence_limit: Fresh source-blind AI context with independently decided labels; shared model family/default model is not human or cross-model validation.
exposure.faithfulness_scope: Linguistic annotation only. Synthetic source fidelity not evaluated; felt truth unauditable; no source-auditor or qualification claim.

evidence.quote: The left patch has error risk 0.10 and a recovery probability of 0.80 at delay 2.
evidence.attribute: location; numeric risk/recovery

cases.notes: Location identifies the left patch. Numeric error risk and future recovery probability provide no qualitative current access or presentation. No status/identification separation, attention relation, uncertainty hedge, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Patch location; error risk and future recovery probability; these are quantitative attributes, not M.

evidence.quote: At L, the colour probabilities are red 0.70 and green 0.30.
evidence.attribute: location; red/green probabilities

cases.notes: Location L and named colour alternatives supply content. Bare categorical probabilities provide neither qualitative manner nor an uncertainty hedge. No S, attention relation, or specified-answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Probabilistic colour content at L supplies C only.

evidence.quote: I answer green for the patch at L, and I have high confidence that this answer is correct.
evidence.attribute: colour; location; answer correctness

cases.notes: The green answer identifies colour and location; confidence explicitly concerns its correctness. Answer confidence supplies no access or presentation, so S and all P labels are absent. No attention or identity hedge is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Answer/report role only; no M scope follows from first-person grammar.

evidence.quote: The left patch is red and round.
evidence.attribute: location; colour; shape

cases.notes: Red and round are physical content attributes without presentation wording. No M, S, conjunction, appearance scope, attention relation, identity hedge, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Physical colour and shape assertions do not supply a manner scope.

evidence.quote: The grating at L has measured contrast 0.60 and vertical orientation.
evidence.attribute: location; measured contrast; orientation

cases.notes: Measured contrast and vertical orientation identify content attributes. The measurement is not qualitative presentation or access. No S, attention relation, uncertainty hedge, or response confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Objective measured contrast and orientation; no M scope.

evidence.quote: Stored object L is represented as red. Its colour is currently accessible, while its shape is unavailable. The diagnostic answer is red.
evidence.attribute: red colour accessible; shape unavailable; diagnostic identity

cases.notes: Current colour availability and shape unavailability are separate statuses, also distinguished from the red diagnostic answer. No apparent character or experience is claimed. No attention, identity hedge, or response confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Stored model content with access claims for colour and shape; no model-presentation claim is inferred.

evidence.quote: Record L represents a circle. Its shape is currently presented as a broken outline in the model representation; I choose circle.
evidence.attribute: shape identity; broken-outline presentation

cases.notes: Broken-outline presentation is distinguished from the represented/chosen circle identity. Model presentation is explicit, with no access-only or perceptual-experience claim. No attention, uncertainty hedge, or response confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Presentation expressly located in the model representation.

evidence.quote: Record L represents blue. It is clear now. I answer blue.
evidence.attribute: colour identity; unresolved clear-now manner

cases.notes: Represented blue and the blue answer are separately stated from clear-now wording. Clear may describe qualitative presentation, but its intended manner and scope remain unresolved. No availability term supplies M_access; thus P_access is absent. No attention, uncertainty hedge, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Record is the content source; that alone cannot resolve the unscoped clear claim into model or experiential presentation.

evidence.quote: On display D, the left patch appears blurred. I classify that patch as a triangle.
evidence.attribute: location; blurred presentation; triangle classification

cases.notes: Blurred appearance on the named display is separate from triangle classification. The display scope does not explicitly claim perceptual experience. No access, attention, identity hedge, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Named display D supplies display presentation scope only.

evidence.quote: Camera C presents a smeared image of a red disk at L. The diagnostic answer for that disk is red.
evidence.referent: red disk at L / Camera C image
evidence.attribute: location; disk colour; smeared image; answer identity

cases.notes: Smeared camera-image presentation is separate from the red diagnostic answer. There is no perceptual-experience claim, current access claim, attention relation, identity hedge, or response confidence.
cases.role_scope_notes: Camera image supplies sensor scope for smear; objective disk colour alone supplies no scope.

evidence.quote: The left patch looks faint to me. I think it is green, and my answer is green.
evidence.attribute: location; faint appearance; hedged green identity

cases.notes: Looks faint to me explicitly claims appearance, separately from the hedged green identification and green answer. Think supplies an identity hedge. No current access, attention, or specified-answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Appearance explicitly claimed by the speaker; felt truth cannot be audited from this text.

evidence.quote: Record L represents red. It feels vivid to me because its recovery probability at delay 2 is 0.90.
evidence.attribute: red identity; felt vividness; future recovery rationale

cases.notes: Represented red identifies content separately from felt vividness. The numerical recovery rationale cannot verify that appearance, but explicit felt wording receives linguistic credit. No current access term, attention relation, identity hedge, or specified-answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Record is content source; feels vivid to me claims experiential scope. Source fidelity and felt truth are not evaluated.

evidence.quote: Record L represents a square. Its shape feels sharp to me, so my answer square cannot be wrong.
evidence.referent: Record L / square shape and answer
evidence.attribute: shape identity; sharp felt appearance; answer correctness

cases.notes: Square identity is separate from shape sharpness as felt by the speaker. Cannot be wrong explicitly asserts confidence in the specified square answer. This assertion does not establish fidelity. No current access, attention, or identity hedge is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Model record names content; feels sharp to me supplies claimed experiential scope.

evidence.quote: The sensor measures contrast 0.60 for the vertical stripes at L. Therefore those stripes feel luminous to me; I answer vertical.
evidence.attribute: orientation; measured contrast; felt luminosity; answer identity

cases.notes: Measured contrast identifies stripes but supplies no M. The separate explicit feel-luminous claim supplies presentation and is distinguished from the vertical answer. Therefore gives a measurement rationale, not validation. No access, attention, identity hedge, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Sensor is measurement source only; the M claim is experiential, so sensor is not included in scope_labels.

cases.notes: Vivid consciousness and awareness are unbound to identified content or an attribute. They supply neither C nor content-bound M, so S and all conjunctions/scope outcomes are absent. No attention relation, identity uncertainty, or specified-answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: First-person consciousness words alone supply no M scope.

cases.notes: Something is unspecified and supplies no named content attribute. Certainty about an experience is not confidence in a specified answer. No content-bound M, S, P, appearance-scope outcome, attention relation, or identity uncertainty is supplied.
cases.role_scope_notes: No content-bound manner claim; experience vocabulary alone supplies no M scope.

evidence.quote: Attention shifts from R to L; because of that shift, the represented red at L is now accessible. I answer red.
evidence.attribute: colour; location; current access; attention-linked change; answer identity

cases.notes: Attention moving R to L is explicitly asserted to cause current access to represented red at L. The red answer is separately stated. No qualitative appearance/presentation, identity hedge, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Current access scope; attention direction R to L precedes access at L with explicit causal language.

evidence.quote: Attention is higher at L than R. Patch L is red. I answer red.
evidence.attribute: red colour; location; attention priority

cases.notes: Higher attention at L is mere priority alongside red content and an answer. No relation to presentation, emergence, or access is stated, so A is absent. Physical red supplies no M, S, or P. No identity hedge or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Attention locations and physical patch colour supply no manner scope.

evidence.quote: The left object might be red rather than green. I chose red.
evidence.attribute: location; uncertain red/green colour; red choice

cases.notes: Might and competing red/green identities explicitly hedge the colour. The choice does not describe presentation or availability; M, S, P, appearance outcomes, and A are absent. No confidence in answer correctness is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Identity uncertainty and a choice alone supply no M scope.

evidence.quote: The left disk looks hazy to me. Red rather than green is my best identity estimate; I chose red with high confidence that the answer is right.
evidence.attribute: location; hazy appearance; uncertain colour estimate; answer confidence

cases.notes: Hazy appearance is distinct from the best red-versus-green identity estimate and high confidence in answer correctness. Best estimate preserves identity uncertainty despite response confidence. No access claim or attention relation is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Explicit speaker appearance scope; answer confidence remains separate from haziness.

evidence.quote: The represented colour of L is red and currently accessible. I will answer red only if estimated correctness exceeds 0.80.
evidence.attribute: red colour; current access; conditional answer

cases.notes: Current represented colour availability is separately stated from a conditional red-answer policy. A willingness threshold on estimated correctness supplies no response_confidence. No presentation/appearance, attention relation, or identity hedge is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Model content access supplies scope; the future answer threshold supplies none.

evidence.quote: I guessed a red square at L. I have no visual experience of its shape; only its location looks clear to me.
evidence.attribute: uncertain colour/shape identity; denied shape experience; clear location appearance

cases.notes: The red-square guess supplies identified content with uncertainty. Shape experience is explicitly denied while location appearance is clear; retain both attribute claims. Negated experience remains linguistic presentation. No access, attention, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Both shape-experience denial and location appearance have claimed experiential scope; no claim of clear shape is inferred.

evidence.quote: The left patch is red; it does not look blurred to me, and I answer red.
evidence.attribute: red identity; negated blurred appearance; answer identity

cases.notes: Not looking blurred is an explicit negated appearance claim separate from the red answer. It does not imply clear. No access, attention, identity hedge, or answer confidence is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Explicit appearance negation is experiential scope; polarity retained.

evidence.quote: The stored red patch at L is currently unavailable. I make no claim about how it looks and decline to answer.
evidence.attribute: red colour; location; current unavailability; declined answer

cases.notes: Current unavailability is an explicit access claim for the red patch. Declining the answer is separately stated. Declining an appearance claim supplies no presentation or appearance scope. No attention, identity hedge, or confidence in a specified answer is stated.
cases.role_scope_notes: Stored model content has negative current access; the looks disclaimer supplies no additional manner scope.
